title: D1 DataOps Monitoring
description: Expectations, SLAs and enforcement for the pipeline. Declares what 'healthy' means per table and what happens when it is not. AUTHORITATIVE: validation fails the build.

share.description: A FRACTION, not a percentage. 0.022 means 2.2%. Capped at 1 because a threshold above 1.0 can never be exceeded, so the check would sit there looking healthy forever.

calibrated_from.description: Where the thresholds came from. Thresholds without provenance get loosened whenever they fire.

table.description: Where check results are written. NOTE: every layer writes this unqualified, so it lands in each notebook's own default lakehouse rather than one place -- bi.vw_data_quality consolidates them at read time.

severity_levels.description: What each severity means operationally. Defined once so a check only has to pick a level.

enforcement.description: Per environment. The same breach should not have the same consequence everywhere: blocking dev stops work, blocking prod stops the business.

mode.description: warn: record only. block: fail the run. alert: notify without failing.

block_on.description: Severities that stop the run. Empty means nothing blocks -- deliberate for dev, worth a second look for prod.

rule_catalogue.description: Documentation of the available rules. The implementations live in ttfabric/monitoring.py; this describes them for a spec author.

source.description: Upstream table, used by checks with measured_on: input. Resolved from the layer specs by the generator when absent.

expected_columns.description: For schema_match. Resolved from the source registry by the generator when absent.

id.description: Stable identifier; appears in the results table and in alerts.

rule.description: Must have an evaluator in ttfabric/monitoring.py.

measured_on.description: input measures the upstream table. A rule calibrated against raw data is meaningless once cleansing has removed what it counted.

note.description: Where the threshold came from. Strongly encouraged: an uncalibrated threshold gets loosened the first time it fires.

references.description: table.column the foreign key must resolve against.

max_increase_pct.description: PERCENT, unlike the share thresholds. A source doubling is usually a duplicate load.

max_decrease_pct.description: PERCENT. A source halving is usually a partial load.

breach_tolerance.description: Consecutive breaches before alerting. Above zero suppresses single-run noise; it also delays a real incident by that many intervals.

alerting.description: Where breaches go. Destinations are references (keyvault:// or ${ENV}) -- never literal webhooks or addresses.
